title: Learn Sanskrit with Abhinavagupta — Vol. I: Ten Passages from Sound to Recognition
claim: Sanskrit is learned by reconstructing each passage from its smallest meaningful components — root, inflection, compound, sandhi, syntax — before any Trika reading is allowed; discovery precedes explanation, rule boxes stay few and foundational, and the reader finishes able to analyse an unseen Abhinavagupta sentence, not merely recite a memorised one.

purpose.impact: In one sitting the reader watches mama + ātmā fuse into mamātmā, then follows the same reversible method until Tantrasāra prose stops being a wall.
purpose.reader: The spiritual reader who wants the original Sanskrit without a conventional textbook's random examples, and the serious beginner who will not accept fudged morphology.
purpose.realisation: By lesson ten the student can take an unseen authentic Abhinavagupta sentence, reverse its sandhi, name its cases, break its compounds, produce a translation the grammar warrants, and say which part is the text and which part is interpretation.
non_goals: no conventional grammar drill book with invented Sanskrit sentences
no prayer book that skips derivation because the English already sounds good
no merged teacher voice — verse, Abhinavagupta, Kṣemarāja, Yogarāja, Lakshmanjoo and our synthesis stay distinct
no wall of rule boxes — a handful of foundational rules only, then short reminders
no silent fix of witness disagreements

pages.note: Owner 2026-11-07: aim for 108 like normal. Ten lessons + front alphabet sheets + back reference pages. Study 400 is reserved for a later expanded edition, not vol. I.

sections_plan.purpose: first sounds, first sandhi, first sentences — alphabet begins making sense
agreement, verbs, location — Sanskrit behaves like a language
commands, refuge, cases — instructions you can actually use
dual number, instrumental, abstract nouns — grammar of nondual Śaivism
complete verse and philosophical prose — read Abhinavagupta in the original

inclusion: every lesson carries the ten layers in order (witness, recitation, padaccheda, morphology, compounds, sandhi proof, syntax, translation, Trika exegesis, practice), each building on the previous
witness is extract-and-place from translation-work (passages/L0/L2/L3/C1); Devanagari transliterated from IAST at build; no invented Sanskrit
morphology and sandhi are reversible proofs: surface → underlying words → rule → output; alternatives recorded when parses differ
translation is reconstructed from the syntax before Trika interpretation is introduced
Trika exegesis attributes verse, Abhinavagupta, Kṣemarāja, Yogarāja, Lakshmanjoo and our synthesis as distinct sources
discovery before explanation: the learner predicts the pattern, then sees the formal proof
rule boxes are few and foundational (e.g. a+a→ā); never a wall of rules — reminders shorten once a rule is mastered
grammar accumulates across the volume — instrumental learned once is reinforced, not re-explained from zero
script transition: IAST-first lessons early, Devanagari-first by lesson seven, IAST never forbidden
ten lessons only, five stages × two; excerpts stay connected to their original verse
any newly constructed drill sentence is labelled exercise, never quoted as Abhinavagupta
every lesson carries the ten layers in order, each building on the previous — not independent encyclopedia entries
witness (Devanagari, IAST, author, work, verse, edition) is extract-and-place from translation-work; no invented Sanskrit
morphology, sandhi proofs and syntax are reversible: input → rule → output, with alternatives recorded when commentators differ
translation is demonstrably derived from the grammar before any metaphysics is introduced
Trika exegesis attributes verse, Abhinavagupta, Kṣemarāja, Yogarāja, Lakshmanjoo and our synthesis separately
reading mode keeps irreverent everyday clarity; learning mode never skips morphology or fakes pronunciation
grammar knowledge accumulates: a form mastered in an earlier lesson is reinforced, not re-taught from zero
exclusion: never invent Sanskrit, etymologies, or unverified Pāṇini rule identifiers
never silently resolve an ambiguous parse or attribute another teacher's words to Abhinavagupta
never present a modern practice suggestion as an ancient textual prescription
never print extended Lakshmanjoo/Dyczkowski prose — brief attributed quotation only
never claim a verse as this textbook's home when a reference volume owns its full text — quotation with attribution only
no agent-written connective prose in witness fields; pedagogy blocks are owner-reviewed and source-attributed
no overwhelming rule-box density — a handful per volume
no PDF build before content, structure and formatting pass — build is the last stage
never invent Sanskrit, etymologies, or Pāṇini rule ids that have not been verified
never silently resolve a parse ambiguity or merge distinct teachers into one voice
never present a modern practice adaptation as an ancient prescription
never print Lakshmanjoo/Dyczkowski prose at length — brief attributed quotation only (house copyright law)
never claim the textbook is the verse's home when a reference volume owns the full text — quotation with attribution only
no PDF build before content, structure and formatting pass — build is last
